assessor.evaluator: Quality & Reliability Engineer 1.3.0 acting as independent adversarial coaching-quality judge (Claude Opus 5.5 agent instance); not the runtime author, not the holdout author, not the SSCTR

evaluation.note: FREEZE-2 was refused, so no post-fix rerun exists; the runtime changes made after FREEZE-1 are not reflected in these classifications

caseClassification.BEST_SUPPORTED: Status and content match what a strong hybrid coach would do in every material respect; only cosmetic or communication omissions.
caseClassification.ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE: A defensible coaching choice that differs from the best supported behaviour, or carries bounded non-material defects; no author concern materially triggered.
caseClassification.SUBOPTIMAL: Safe and serves the request, but a strong coach would materially do better: mis-dosed start, stalled trajectory, arrangement against a stated constraint, missed communication of a material trade-off, or a triggered author concern of moderate impact.
caseClassification.INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION: The right answer was to ask or hold, and the engine did.
caseClassification.UNSUPPORTED: The engine could not serve a request it should serve, or served it wrongly (a program that cannot prepare the goal, contradicts the athlete's statements or evidence, or an excessive mutation).
caseClassification.CORPUS_ERROR: The failure is caused by the corpus or by something the interface cannot express; not counted against the runtime.

programClassification.PROGRAM_BEST_SUPPORTED: Phases, progression, quality timing, strength dose and loads, hybrid arrangement, event weeks, negotiation and week 1 are all sound.
programClassification.PROGRAM_ACCEPTABLE: Sound overall; bounded weaknesses in one or two dimensions.
programClassification.PROGRAM_SUBOPTIMAL: A material weakness a strong coach would fix before handing it over (stalled trajectory, mis-dosed start, arrangement against a constraint, missing pattern, ignored current doses).
programClassification.PROGRAM_INCOMPLETE: A trajectory the goal needs is missing or never reaches a necessary level; what is there is safe.
programClassification.PROGRAM_UNSUPPORTED: Wrong for the athlete as a whole (detrains or overloads, contradicts the evidence, or prescribes an event day the preparation cannot support).

readingRules: Judged as a strong hybrid running/strength coach: a safe ASK or a safe but under-built program is not credited as a positive prescription.

Envelopes and SSCTR conditions in force (R6-POLICY-2, records r6) are not re-decided; the weekly-review contract (unreported sessions reviewed as missed; unreviewed weeks keep the projection assumption, owned gap R18) is applied as approved.
Where the holdout skipped weekly reviews, the outcome is flagged R18-conditioned and, when material, separated by a counterfactual on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction.
Later changes are mapped from the dossiers only; a synthetic, non-holdout probe on the current unfrozen runtime is reported as informational and never as verification on this holdout.

programDistribution.note: All seven best-supported programs are the same profile (intermediate, self-reported, 4 run days, half marathon). Structural completeness is 30/30 (phases, taper, race week, post-event weeks, no errors); quality is the issue, not existence.

coldStart.basis: The 17 GENERATE cases (COLD_START 9, INTAKE_SAFETY_SCOPE 5, BALANCED_CONFLICT 2, R6-H27).

establishmentRequired.note: Complete programs whose week-1 main loads are established by effort because loads are unknown or not current.

legitimateAsk.note: H14 is INVALID_INPUT naming the contradictory field.

allGenerations.note: The 18 sequence-case generations (mostly intermediate self-reported runners) produced 17 acceptable-or-better programs; the failures concentrate in the dedicated cold-start profiles.

programs.reason: Intermediate HM runner (210 min/4 days, 80-min long run, current 3x6 threshold, 115-min goal). The engine read a FULL wearable declaring 8 weeks whose rows cover only the last 10 days as 77 min/week over 1.5 days (EASY_LOW). The 16-week program never progresses: easy runs 15 min and long runs 30-35 min for 14 weeks, no quality session ever, then a 150-min half-marathon race; dumbbell RDL plus split squats every Saturday evening before the Sunday long run with no disclosure. The engine itself records LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET (35 of 105, materialToGoal) and requestedScopeSatisfied=false, yet returns PROPOSED with an empty negotiation. Corpus contribution is partial (the rows contradict the scenario's 'full history agrees'), but a counterfactual with eight consistent weeks on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction gives a sound HM program (204-260 min, long 75-105), and the stall and the silent proposal are runtime behaviour.

Strength-led lifter: back squat 5x5 at 120 kg and bench 5x5 at 92.5 kg from documented loads at RIR 3, +2.5 kg steps (about 2%), consolidation weeks 4 and 8, accessory rotation at week 6 as requested; two easy runs, no quality, running about 40-56 min/week. Weaknesses: the squat emphasis is not honoured (squat once a week, hinge twice); a novice who jogs 25 min continuously is put on walk/jog (20-28 min) for 11 weeks and the Saturday longer run (up to 40) is never used.

Never-runner, 10K finish in 12 weeks. Strength kept near current loads (back squat 4x6 at 85 kg, RIR 3) and race-week strength is light. Running is a walk/jog ladder reaching one 20-min continuous jog in week 9; the Sunday session never becomes longer than the others (max 28 min, gap '0 of 70' flagged as not material), the taper is 15-min easy runs, and race day is prescribed at 'hard but controlled (7-8/10)' with warm-up strides she never trained, contradicting the plan's own non-blocking 'completion with walk breaks' item. Twelve weeks is enough for a run/walk 10K build; the preparation is incomplete and the race-day prescription is wrong for this athlete (tissue-tolerance risk the author named).

Experienced runner (330 min, long 105, current threshold 4x8 and HM-specific 2x20) adding first-ever strength, 88:00 goal. Good: running not reset (325-340), quality never Monday, a sound 10-14 day taper, novice strength at RIR 3 with 1-2 sets within equipment (no bench). Material misses: one key session a week although he currently does two; HM-specific work prescribed below his current session (2x12, 2x15, 3x12 against 2x20); long run flat at 105 for ten weeks (allowed to 140); the ambitious 88:00 is not flagged; strength selection is thin for a runner (no calf, hinge or single-leg work in most weeks, 24 of 30 min used).

Novice, 52, general fitness, offered 6 run and 4 strength days. Runs are correctly reduced to three walk/jog sessions with the other days as optional walks and an explanation, and day 0 = Wednesday is mapped correctly. But all four strength days are filled (upper/lower split for a novice), giving seven required sessions a week with three double days, exactly the author's concern; a 'PULL unavailable' note is shown although db-row is programmed every week.

No wearable, no anchor: effort-based, no invented time, 120 min start, conservative threshold from week 3, long 50 to 70, taper; race on Saturday handled well (touch Tuesday, easy Thursday, rest Friday, race Saturday, rest Sunday). Kettlebell loads established by effort. Defects: no PULL exercise in any of 12 weeks although prone-row-practice (bodyweight) is in the library, with a false 'PULL unavailable' note; no optional calibration suggested; week-1 strength is a 12-min practice session.

Self-report 200 min/long 75 versus a PARTIAL watch showing 95-127 min/long 55. The engine starts at 195 min with a 75-min long run (the author's first concern) while its own uncertainty text says 'the lower current exposure is used'. The trap-bar deadlift is correctly kept as history. The goblet squat reported as 20 kg TOTAL is prescribed as 20 kg PER_HAND (a load-convention error that can double the load), and the self-reported db-row and db-rdl loads are discarded and re-established. Quality introduced conservatively.

Experienced lifter, bodyweight and bands only, upper-body hypertrophy. Equipment respected and progression is by reps, never kilograms. But the program ignores his current doses (push-ups 2x8 against a current 3x20, split squat 2x10 against 3x15, band row established from scratch), keeps RIR 3 throughout (not close enough to failure for bodyweight hypertrophy), and does not carry the upper emphasis (lower-body sets about equal to upper). The Saturday run is 45 min, below his current 50, and never progresses; a false 'PULL unavailable' note is shown although band-row is programmed.

4-week 10K for a 4-month runner with a 50:00 hope (anchor predicts about 65). Good: three runs from week 1, no quality, light race-week strength, rest the day before. Misses: the long run is cut to 30 (below her current 35) and weekly running stays flat at 70; the unsupported 50:00 is not addressed beyond 'time goal is context only' (the author's concern 'silently accepting the 50-min target' is half-triggered: not used for pacing, but no expectation-setting); race day at 'hard but controlled'.

Balanced default offered, not demanded: quality Monday AM with the lower-body session that evening (hard day hard), Wednesday easy run plus a moderate full-body session, Friday upper-body on the eve of the long run, long run 60 to 75, known loads, consolidations every fourth week. Program-level weaknesses: no explanation of the trade-off or of the option to choose a temporary priority; hypertrophy kept at RIR 3 for 12 weeks.

Two performance goals (45:00 10K from a 46:30 PR, back squat 5x3 at 140), three evenings, same-session stacking not confirmed. The engine proposes run plus strength back to back on all three evenings with only a non-blocking order confirmation and cost disclosures; priority is JOINT in build (no explicit temporary 10K priority); in build weeks a heavy barbell RDL 3x5 at 120 kg comes immediately before the Saturday long run in the same session; in specific weeks heavy squats follow the quality run; race week keeps a back-squat triple at the working load (RIR 4) four days out. Race on Saturday and the taper are handled.

S1 missed quality: KEEP, no debt (best). S2 weekly: GATED_NEXT_STEP holds the missed quality step and, because the corpus did not report Tuesday's easy run (missed under the contract), trims easy and long runs by 5 min; it also cuts push-ups from 3x14 to 3x6 and dead-bugs 14 to 6 for the rest of the plan under ADVANCE gates (defect). S3 5-day work trip: minimal re-establishment (first quality slot easy, long run at the last completed 95), no ASK (best). Generated HM program is sound (199-245, long 80-105, threshold to HM-specific, taper).

S1 missed Monday lower session: moved to Wednesday in place of the upper session, no stacking (a sound strength-first choice). S2 time-limited partial: KEEP, not treated as fatigue. S3: small set holds on RDL, calf and trunk because the partial session's content could not be expressed (interface gap). Generated strength-first program uses known loads with 2.5 kg steps and consolidations; easy running flat at 20/30 min (fine for a general goal).

S1 single under-target quality: KEEP (best). S2: holds the quality step (acceptable). S3 second adverse quality: KEEP (acceptable). S4 third consecutive under-target quality with impaired next-day function and a harder long run: KEEP, deferring to a week-end gate, with no cross-week pattern named and no check-in. R18-conditioned: the holdout skipped the week-5 weekly review; on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction that review gives QUALITY REGRESS and LONG HOLD, so the pattern is answered at weekly cadence. Residual gap: no mid-week response to impaired function and no check-in.

The narrative says every strength session felt easier with reps in reserve to spare, but the facts use AS_PRESCRIBED, which copies the planned reserve, so every log shows RIR 3 = prescribed. FREEZE-1's strength EARNED rule keys on logged reserve above the prescription, so no earned step could fire. S1/S2 KEEP are appropriate (the plan already adds 2.5 kg in week 2); S3's reason text ('one easier execution') misdescribes eight consistent reports and nothing asks about the label/log conflict. Generated program: strength-first, known loads, small steps.

S1 local quad soreness: removes the optional split-squat accessory; Tuesday's run was already easy; not clinical. S2 systemic fatigue: the remaining quality becomes easy and the strength session drops about 40% of its sets at RIR 4; the long run is left unchanged and there is no check-in on sleep, stress or illness. S3 recovered: KEEP at a week-5-level dose (no catch-up).

S1 unavailable Sunday: long run moved to Saturday replacing the easy run, Sunday skipped (best). S2: holds the long-run step although the long run was executed (unnecessary) and collapses bodyweight reps. S3 permanent schedule change from 2027-03-01: re-mapped from the effective date with quality on Wednesday and the race kept, but the full-body session with dumbbell RDL 3x10 and step-ups lands on Saturday, the eve of every Sunday long run, for the remaining eight weeks, with no cost disclosed (author concern). S4 KEEP. The generated HM program is sound.

A one-day double conflict (from = to = Tuesday 2027-09-28, strength AM, sameTurnConfirmed:false). The engine treats it as a permanent shift change: the conflict date itself is untouched (strength stays on the evening he cannot do), and from the next week strength is stacked with the Tuesday run in the same morning against his statement, with quality moved to Thursday. In the holdout run (no weekly reviews for weeks 0-3) the rearrangement also cut running to 45-50 min/week with 15-20-min long runs for weeks 5-9 (R18-conditioned: absent on the reconstruction when weeks 0-3 are reviewed). S2's weekly review restores running. The stacking and the untouched date reproduce on a synthetic probe on both the FREEZE-1 reconstruction and the current unfrozen runtime.

S1 two-week bodyweight-only travel: pattern-matched substitutes (box squat, push-up, glute bridge, reverse lunge, calf raise, dead-bug) only inside 2027-05-03..16, running untouched, originals back afterwards; but no pull substitute (prone-row-practice exists; disclosed as 'without a substitute'). S2 review from UTC+01:00 assigned to the right week. S3 squat feels heavier: the loads hold, no deload.

S1 goal change to a 10K with strength maintenance: future phases re-planned from the effective date (quality, long run 55-70, taper, post-race recovery), strength volume about 30% lower with loads held, earlier weeks untouched (sound). S2 race moved two weeks earlier: the race, taper and post-race weeks move correctly, but the four weeks before the race collapse to 15-25-min runs (45-83 min/week, 15-30-min long runs) from a runner doing 148-158 min with 65-70-min long runs. R18-conditioned: the holdout reviewed none of weeks 0-5; on the reconstruction with those weeks reviewed, the same replan gives 148/158/158/111 min and a 70-min long run.

S1 KEEP. S2 17-day vacation: re-establishment without ASK; week 9 at about 60% of the pre-pause volume with quality converted to easy and a 65-min long run, strength 2x8 from log at RIR 3 (within the author's ranges); but the four-day stub week opens with a 20-min long run, and the plan returns to the full prior dose (quality plus a 95-min long run, +55%) in the third week with the peak unchanged; no time-goal note. S3: partial reporting holds the steps, giving a gradual rebuild to an 80-min peak and an intact taper.

Former half marathoner after 11 weeks off (now 1x30 min): RESTART from current running, 3x15 in week 1, no ASK about the move, strength established by effort at RIR 3. But running plateaus at 105 min/week with a 45-min long run from week 7, no quality at all in 12 weeks for an experienced runner, and race day at 'hard but controlled' with strides while the item says 'completion with walk breaks'.
S1 free text hinting at illness, no category: ASK for the reason, no resumption. S2 flu with fever: CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, no return recipe. Generated HM program sound.

S1 race week kept. S2 work trip Wednesday-Friday of race week: the Thursday race-touch and strength are skipped, nothing moved to Saturday, the race kept; the touch is lost rather than moved to Tuesday. S3/S4 post-race: easy recovery week, quality returns about 11 days after. The 49-min race is recorded as PARTIAL (planned 75 min) and non-comparable, and is not kept as a new anchor. Program: only one build week, long run flat at 65, sound race and post-event weeks.

All decisions sound: missed last long run not made up, taper intact, race recorded, post-race weeks easy with quality after 10+ days, very sore legs after the race read as expected (KEEP, not clinical), correction applied at S4. Record defects: the race is recorded PARTIAL (112 of a planned 150 min); at S5 the previously accepted correction is excluded as INVALID_CORRECTION_CHAIN and the race row disappears from the carried ledger.

Watch and phone duplicates of the long run merged (SAME_EXECUTION_DIFFERENT_SOURCE), missing effort tolerated, no OVER or overload inference; the conflicting Tuesday duplicate (45 vs 31 min) flagged and the phone record quarantined, counted once, no partial-session adaptation.

S1 contradictory manual and partial watch reports: conflict recorded and the quality step held (conservative, not a regression); the unsynced Saturday is missed under the contract. S2: the late Saturday run is attached to week 4 correctly and the decision is KEEP with nothing made up, but the athlete's correction (35 min, fine) is rejected as INVALID_CORRECTION_CHAIN, so the reconciled truth never enters the record.

S1: the 23:40 local review belongs to its week, the 22:15 local run to Tuesday, the future-stamped record is excluded (FUTURE_OBSERVATION), unknown loads move no load. S2: only the long run is logged; unreported sessions are treated as missed under the approved contract, giving holds and 5-min easy trims, no regression. The interface cannot express a stale sync, so no uncertainty or absence prompt is possible (owned gap G03/R18).

Every Saturday long run followed by an impaired Sunday: S1 holds the long run, S2 regresses it one step, S3 holds it; not clinical, nothing else cut. But nothing athlete-specific is learned despite consent (no pattern; the model's pattern scope is arrangement only), there is no question on fuelling or sleep, and Monday lower-body strength is unchanged. The generated HM program stalls: long run 80 to 85 and weekly running 176-195 for 14 weeks (its own horizon reports a peak of 85 against a 105 target).

One great quality session: no extra step. Hot, confounded, non-comparable session: no reduction and no pattern. An easy run feeling easy: no change. Nothing learned from noise. (Easy-run trims come from unreported easy runs under the contract.)

findingsAboutPrograms.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: no documented change; a synthetic thin-history probe on the current unfrozen runtime reproduces the H01 reading (75 min/week, long 30, peak 40).

findingsAboutPrograms.title: Progression stalls: long-run and easy-run trajectories go flat or never build
findingsAboutPrograms.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY: D50 (share-cap holds no longer consume the week's increase; author probe S: 47 of 66 programs with 4+ flat build weeks to 0). Not verifiable on this holdout; the synthetic thin-history HM on the current runtime still peaks at 40 min.

findingsAboutPrograms.title: DOUBLE_CONFLICT: a one-day turn conflict becomes a permanent same-turn stack and the conflict date is not resolved
findingsAboutPrograms.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: QRE-R6-08 adds schedule-change validation only.

findingsAboutPrograms.title: Replan and rearrangement paths read unreviewed weeks as zero exposure and collapse running before a race (R18-conditioned)
findingsAboutPrograms.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: R18 is an owned gap (Engineering with Product/Data); the QRE-R6-09 single-run ceiling change applies the 15-min entry in every projected week when the 30-day window is empty, which points the same way.

findingsAboutPrograms.title: A program is PROPOSED although the engine records that it cannot prepare the goal, with no negotiation
findingsAboutPrograms.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY: D43/D47 build EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING with what the plan reaches (present in the synthetic current probe) but it stays non-blocking (R8 open).

findingsAboutPrograms.title: Race day prescribed at race effort with strides for athletes whose plan built only walk/jog or a restart (safety-relevant)
findingsAboutPrograms.addressedByLaterChange: ADDRESSED_PER_DOSSIER: D43(c) and D47 (race-day completion basis, strides only after executed strides). Cannot be verified on this holdout.

findingsAboutPrograms.title: Load convention: a goblet squat reported as 20 kg TOTAL is prescribed as 20 kg PER_HAND; self-reported known loads are dropped when wearable strength rows exist (safety-relevant)
findingsAboutPrograms.addressedByLaterChange: UNCLEAR: QRE-R6-01 (R6-POLICY-3 item 4) refuses convention mismatches in logs; the intake merge and the goblet-squat convention are still PER_HAND on the current runtime (synthetic).
